title: Seminar Market's neighbours and the alley bands
summary: He details the stores around the market and the little bands that played in the alley bar, such as Maurice Durand's group with Frazier's drummer colleague.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, well the Circle was a grocery store, but it first started to crawl down. The first Seminar Market, I can remember, it wasn't named, it was called, you had the butcher stands, and you had the vegetable stand to the front part of the building, and across the street from there where you see a brick building, that used to be Maggie Gagne's hardware store. You see that brick, and when that caught a fire, years back, I forgot this was year that happened, when that caught, and during that same time the fire they had like a rain, a rain flood. It flood the street, the wall almost up to the side steps on the sidewalk. Well Maggie Gagne had the hardware store there for years and years, and next to the Seminar Market used to be the alley, and next to the alley had a feed store there, you see, and all those new buildings come up there, and then come two little single white houses, you see, and some of the houses still stands there, outside of the alley is gone, because it's the door. Then next to the Seminar Market too, during them days, they had like a two-story building, it was down there called Steinmann, the Jewish guy had a dry goods store, like a notion store there, called Steinmann's, you see, and then when you go between the market and Steinmann's a notion store, you had the alley, it was run by these people here called, they used to run the old lottery shops, the Andre Dominguez. The Dominguez? Yeah, Andre Dominguez. I've never heard of that. Yeah, they look like Spanish type people, Andre Dominguez. Let me see, wait now. Yeah, you know that stuff, but I think it was Andre Dominguez. Well they lived there for years and years on the street called North Romant between Seminar and New Orleans Street, yeah. They stood there for, now that same house where they was living at, they took that house and they made it like a apartment. Yeah, they made it that distance to that, on North Romant Street. But the alley, doing it, was in full blowing during them days, and such bands like Moorish Duran, and playing the trumpet, a fellow by the name, George, he's still living, do a drummer by the name of, I said, Jen, you've got to run that over here, because I can't think of them guys' names. Yeah, and I don't know him, so I can't, but I can't help you. Yeah, I know you don't know him, but I'm trying to play the drum then. Then we had Dodon on banjo, Moorish Duran trumpet, and this boy by the name of George Sutton playing the drum. He was playing, sometimes this kind of little four or five piece band, you'd do an alley there.
And, yeah, yeah, and you would play just around in this little section?
